verdict.rationale: The only licensing evidence is a community report that Mastra's source is published under the Elastic License v2. That makes the source readable, but the license forbids offering the software as a hosted or managed service, so it is source-available rather than an OSI-style open license. The commenter disputes the 'open-source' label, but the pack contains no first-party license documentation to test the claim against. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the license and source repository, an OSI-approved open license without the hosted-service restriction, independent corroboration of the license terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Mastra uses the Elastic v2 license, which forbids providing the software as a hosted or managed service
